chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Hayri from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Hadhrami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in the early period of the caliphate of Abu Ja'far, so he settled in Najaf. He said: 'O Musa, go to the main road and stand on the road and look, for a man will come to you from the direction of al-Qadisiyyah. When he draws near to you, say to him:
Here is a man from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who invites you.
He will come with you.

He said: So I went until I stood on the road, and the heat was intense. I did not cease standing until I nearly went blind, and I was about to leave and leave him, when I looked at something approaching, resembling a man on a camel.

He said: So I did not cease looking at him until he drew near to me. I said to him: 'O this man, here is a man from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who invites you, and he has described you to me.'
He said: 'Take us to him.'
He said: So I brought him to him until he made his camel rest on a side near the tent.
He said: So he called for him, and the Arab entered to him. And I drew near and became at the door of the tent, hearing the speech but not seeing them.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From where did you arrive?'
He said: 'From the farthest part of Yemen.'
He said: 'Are you from such and such a place?'
He said: 'Yes, I am from such and such a place.'
He said: 'Why did you come here?'
He said: 'I came to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So you came for no need other than the visitation.'
He said: 'I came for no need, except that I pray near him, and visit him, and send greetings to him, and return to my family.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And what do you see regarding his visitation?'
He said: 'We see in his visitation the blessing in our selves, our families, our children, our wealth, our livelihoods, and the fulfillment of our needs.'
He said: Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Shall I not add to you from his virtue a virtue, O brother of Yemen?'
He said: 'Add to me, O son of the Messenger of Allah.'
He said: 'The visitation of my Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) equals an accepted, accepted, pure Hajj alongside the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
So he was amazed by that and said: 'Yes, by Allah, two accepted, accepted, pure Hajjs alongside the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

So he was amazed by that, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did not cease adding until he said: 'Thirty accepted, accepted, pure Hajjs alongside the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual elevation of the Zaynabiyya (Imam al-Husayn) shrine during the early Abbasid period, illustrating how sincere visitation serves as a means of connecting with the Ahl al-Bayt's legacy. The Imam’s progressive revelation of the reward—culminating in thirty accepted Hajjs—underscores the unique status of Imam al-Husayn’s burial place as a focal point for divine mercy and intercession in Shia piety.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 40. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Ahmad b. Idris from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. al-Hussain from Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Hayri from Musa b. al-Qasim al-Hadhrami who said:
“The reward is equal to that of thirty accepted and holy Hajjs performed alongside the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.).”
